item: The in-memory keyword rollup build no longer holds the corpus in memory, stages 490 times faster, stops on the memory guard, and a killed build is not restarted identically
summary: Diagnostics of 2026-10-06: on eight 4.81 GiB VMs the build was killed by the kernel 12 times in 4.7 days and restarted identically after every restart (about 2,000 bytes a keyword as ORM entities in one list, 7.5 to 8.8 GB for 3.8 to 4.4 million keywords; executemany staging at 1.1 thousand rows/s). The keyword projection now streams as a column-projected keyset, and both streams go into DuckDB as JSON column arrays in one statement (563 thousand rows/s measured, no new dependency, no file written). The guard is polled after every batch; a start check compares DuckDB's limit, one batch and the guard's floor with available memory; an in-progress marker in the data dir turns a killed build into a declined one (last_build_killed) until the machine has what the dead process held; an encrypted corpus gets no DuckDB offload directory, a plaintext one a per-process folder swept at the next start. Also from the coordinator's check of PR #1305: the slow-step warning is logged while the step runs, a build thread that cannot start releases the lock, and a BaseException is not recorded as done.
